key_insight: Embodied-BenchForge introduces a closed-loop agentic workflow that automates embodied benchmark construction while checking intermediate artifacts at each step. This helps prevent small errors from cascading into faulty final benchmarks.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the difficulty of building embodied benchmarks end-to-end with agents, especially when existing methods only handle isolated stages, depend on specific environments, and fail to verify intermediate outputs before passing them downstream.
method: Uses an agentic, closed-loop pipeline to automate multi-step embodied benchmark creation.
Adds artifact-specific verification for intermediate outputs so defects are caught early.
Supports more general benchmark construction rather than being limited to a fixed environment or task family.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means faster and more reliable benchmark creation for embodied AI systems. It can improve evaluation quality by reducing error propagation and making benchmark generation more scalable and robust.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the multi-step benchmark construction workflow with feedback loops
A comparison graphic contrasting traditional one-pass construction vs. closed-loop verification
Icons for artifacts, validation checks, and error propagation
A before/after chart showing reduced defects in final benchmark outputs
paper_title: Embodied-BenchForge: A Closed-Loop Agentic Workflow for Embodied Benchmark Construction
paper_authors: Baoyang Jiang, Fengchun Zhang, Leyuan Wang, Haotian Li, Yida Wang
